newsitem.title: UK: LME markets end off highs, most still steadier.
newsitem.headline: LME markets end off highs, most still steadier.

text.p: Base metal markets continued to settle back from early peaks during generally routine LME afternoon trading on Thursday but most still finished higher.
Dealers said a pull-back in copper as spread rates eased and a profit-taking reaction in high-flying zinc were matched by the other markets.

Copper prices spent the session consolidating the late upmove seen on Wednesday with business in a broad $2,400/2,420 range. With backwardation rates for the full cash/threes backwardation and some of the sensitive July dates easing slightly, the market tended to gravitate towards the lower end of the band, they said.
However, the bias remains to the upside, given the tightness from the July date to the end of July that will become prominent in the run-up to "third Wednesday".
Last three months business was at $2,404, still up $14 from yesterday's kerb.
Zinc was unable to re-challenge the peak of $1,495 hit this morning as continued profit-taking pushed prices back.
The reaction was unsurprising after gains of some $150 in the last week. Prices ended at $1,476, up $13.
Traders see the downmove as fairly restricted, given forthcoming tightness later in the third quarter, with major shorts finding stocks tightly controlled.
Aluminium also stepped back from highs near $1,620 amid expectations of producer sales. However, there was reasonable buying near $1,600, and final trade at $1,605.50 was just $4.50 down.
Nickel prices drifted back towards the lower end of the day's range after early failing above $7,000 but final trade at $6,930 was only just $10 down from Wednesday.
Lead traded in a narrow, albeit steadier band, closing just below $640 at $639, up $7.
Tin was lacklustre, closing at $5,530, down $5 while alloy was quoted at $1,455/60. --Martin Hayes, London Newsroom 44 171 542 8080
